NDT training in Chicago: how it works for Chicago employers and technicians

Short answer: NDT training for Chicago technicians follows ASNT SNT-TC-1A. Your employer's written practice governs certification: you complete classroom training for the method and level, build documented on-the-job experience, pass general, specific and practical exams under a Level III, and pass an annual vision test. Atlantis NDT delivers Level I, II and III training live online or onsite at your Chicagoland facility, not at a local classroom.

Chicagoland is one of the most varied NDT markets in North America. Within a two-hour drive of the Loop you find large refineries at Joliet, Lemont and Whiting, the biggest concentration of commercial nuclear reactors in the United States, integrated steel mills around the south end of Lake Michigan, heavy-equipment and agricultural-machinery plants, aerospace component makers around Rockford, a dense web of crude, product and natural-gas pipelines, and a city bridge network that includes dozens of movable bridges over the Chicago River. A technician who understands which codes each of those owners works to becomes employable far beyond a single shop.

This section goes deeper than the overview above: method-by-method course content, the SNT-TC-1A steps in order, delivery options that fit around turnarounds and outages, the Illinois radiography certification rules that catch out newcomers, and the Level III support a Chicago employer needs to stay audit-ready. For the national overview see our NDT training programmes.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in Chicago

All courses follow the SNT-TC-1A recommended practice and the body of knowledge used by Level III examiners. Individuals join live online cohorts; employers can book closed groups delivered at their own plant or shop. Senior technicians can add ASNT Level III exam preparation.

MethodLevelsWhat Chicago employers use it forPrerequisite
Ultrasonic Testing (UT)I, II, IIICorrosion and thickness surveys at refineries, weld examination on pressure vessels and structural steel, plate and forging inspection at steel millsLevel I: employer requirements only. Level II: Level I training and experience per written practice
Phased Array UT (PAUT)II, IIIEncoded weld examination on vessels and piping, pipeline girth welds, and heavy-equipment weldments where RT is impracticalConventional UT background normally required
Time-of-Flight Diffraction (TOFD)II, IIICrack sizing and thick-wall weld examination on refinery vessels and reactor componentsConventional UT background
Radiographic Testing (RT)I, II, IIIPipeline and plant piping welds, castings, and interpretation for fabrication shopsIllinois radiographer certification applies to anyone performing source radiography, in addition to SNT-TC-1A
Magnetic Particle Testing (MT)I, II, IIIWeld and component inspection at heavy-equipment plants, steel mills and structural fabricators; wet fluorescent bench work on forgingsEmployer requirements only for Level I
Liquid Penetrant Testing (PT)I, II, IIIStainless piping, aluminium and aerospace parts, pump and valve componentsEmployer requirements only for Level I
Visual Testing (VT)I, II, IIIWeld visual inspection to AWS D1.1 and D1.5, bridge condition inspection, refinery equipment walk-downsVision test and employer requirements
Eddy Current Testing (ET)I, II, IIIHeat-exchanger tube inspection at refineries and power plants, aerospace component and engine inspectionEmployer requirements only for Level I; Level II builds on Level I

Chicago-specific advice: technicians aiming at refinery and pipeline work should plan for UT and RT at Level II, then add PAUT. Those targeting the heavy-equipment and steel sector get the fastest return from MT and UT. Technicians supplying the Rockford aerospace cluster or airline maintenance at O'Hare should look at PT, ET and UT, and expect the employer to apply an aerospace qualification standard such as NAS 410 on top of their training. To map a path for your situation, request a Chicago training quote and tell us which sector you want to work in.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Chicago, step by step

SNT-TC-1A is a recommended practice published by ASNT. It is not a government licence and there is no central SNT-TC-1A card. The employer certifies, and the written practice sets the rules. The steps below apply whether you work for a refinery contractor in Joliet or a two-person fabrication shop in Elk Grove Village.

  1. Employer written practice. Your employer adopts a written practice specifying levels, training, experience, examinations, vision testing and recertification for each method it certifies.
  2. Formal classroom training. You complete documented training for the method and level. Hours are set in the written practice, usually based on SNT-TC-1A recommendations; the training requirements matrix lists the reference figures by method and level.
  3. On-the-job experience. You accumulate documented, supervised experience in the method, signed off by your supervisor or Level III.
  4. General examination. A written theory examination on the method.
  5. Specific examination. A written test on your employer's equipment, procedures and the codes you apply, such as ASME Section V techniques with ASME Section VIII or B31.3 acceptance criteria, API 1104 for pipelines, or AWS D1.1 for structural work.
  6. Practical examination. Hands-on testing of real specimens with known flaws, administered and graded under a Level III.
  7. Vision examination. Near-vision acuity and colour contrast, repeated annually.
  8. Certification. The employer issues certification based on the Level III's evaluation and keeps the records on file for audits.
  9. Recertification. At the interval defined in the written practice, and whenever you move to a new employer.

Because certification stays with the employer, Chicago technicians who move between refinery contractors, mill contractors and fabricators should keep their own copies of training certificates, exam results and experience logs. A new employer's Level III can then credit them quickly. More detail is in our SNT-TC-1A certification guide.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Chicago crews

Atlantis NDT has no physical training centre in Chicago or elsewhere in Illinois. Training is delivered in formats that suit the way Chicagoland employers operate.

Live online. Instructor-led theory sessions for every method and level, joined from home or the workplace. Useful for individuals, for night-shift workers at mills and plants, and for employers that cannot pull a crew off production. See online NDT training.

Onsite at your facility. Closed-group training at your plant, shop or yard under ASNT Level III oversight. Trainees work on your equipment and procedures and, where appropriate, your own reference specimens. For employers with several technicians this is usually the most efficient option; see corporate NDT training.

Scheduling around turnarounds and outages. Chicagoland refineries run planned turnarounds that pull every available technician into the plant for weeks, commonly in spring and autumn. Nuclear plants schedule refuelling outages that do the same for their contractors. Steel mills plan maintenance outages on blast furnaces and rolling lines. Outdoor bridge and pipeline work slows in the Chicago winter. The practical answer is to train in the gaps: many contractors use December to February for classroom work and onsite practicals, then send newly certified technicians into the spring season. Give us your blackout dates and ask about onsite training for your Chicago crew; cohort and onsite quotes come back within one business day.

Where NDT technicians work in Chicago

  • Refining. ExxonMobil's Joliet refinery and CITGO's Lemont refinery lie southwest of the city, and BP's Whiting refinery in northwest Indiana is the largest in the Midwest. In-service inspection of vessels, piping and tanks follows API standards; new construction and repairs follow ASME Section VIII and B31.3. Contractors look for UT, RT and increasingly PAUT at Level II.
  • Nuclear power. Illinois has more operating nuclear reactors than any other state, at Braidwood, Byron, Dresden, LaSalle, Quad Cities and Clinton. In-service inspection follows ASME Section XI, and UT examinations on many components also require performance demonstration qualification under the plant's programme. SNT-TC-1A training is the foundation; plant-specific qualification comes on top.
  • Steel. Integrated mills at Gary, Burns Harbor and Indiana Harbor on the Indiana shore, plus processors and service centres throughout the south suburbs, need UT for plate and billet, MT for crane and rolling-mill components, and ongoing maintenance inspection.
  • Heavy equipment and manufacturing. Caterpillar plants in the Joliet, Aurora and Peoria areas, Deere in the Quad Cities, and hundreds of fabrication shops across Cook, DuPage and Will counties build weldments and castings inspected with MT, UT and VT, usually to AWS D1.1 or customer specifications.
  • Aerospace and aviation. Rockford is home to major aerospace component makers, and airline maintenance operations at O'Hare and Midway require PT, ET, UT and VT, with personnel usually qualified to NAS 410 or the airline's own programme.
  • Pipelines and gas distribution. Chicago is a major crossroads for crude and natural gas pipelines, and the local gas utilities run long-term main replacement programmes. Welding and inspection follow API 1104 and federal pipeline safety rules, with RT and increasingly automated UT on girth welds.
  • Bridges and infrastructure. The Chicago Department of Transportation maintains dozens of movable bascule bridges over the Chicago River, and IDOT and the Illinois Tollway own a large inventory of steel highway bridges. Fatigue-sensitive details are inspected with UT, MT and VT; bridge fabrication follows AWS D1.5.

Radiography licensing in Illinois. Illinois is an NRC Agreement State. The radiation programme at the Illinois Emergency Management Agency and Office of Homeland Security (IEMA-OHS) licenses companies that perform industrial radiography, and Illinois also certifies individual industrial radiographers. Anyone performing or personally supervising industrial radiography in Illinois needs that state certification, which involves a radiation safety examination and an application endorsed by the licensee's radiation safety officer. Working without it is an offence under the Illinois Radiation Protection Act. Note the neighbouring-state trap for Chicagoland crews: northwest Indiana is not an Agreement State, so radiography at Whiting or the Indiana steel mills falls under NRC rules instead. SNT-TC-1A RT training covers technique and film or digital interpretation, not these radiation safety requirements.

Boilers and pressure vessels. Illinois boiler and pressure vessel safety is administered by the Office of the State Fire Marshal, and ASME Code work in the state is examined by personnel certified under a documented written practice. Local employers most often ask for Level II in two or more methods, documented training and experience, and familiarity with the codes named in their contracts. For earnings context see our NDT salary guide.

Level III services and written practices for Chicago NDT companies

Chicagoland has a large base of small and mid-sized fabricators and machine shops that perform NDT as part of manufacturing rather than as their core business. Many run on an outdated written practice, an informal arrangement with a retired Level III, or nothing at all. The problem tends to surface when a new customer, an ASME Code audit, or an aerospace supplier questionnaire asks for evidence.

  • Written practice development. A written practice drafted around your actual methods, levels, customers and codes, with forms for training, experience, examinations and vision records. See written practice development.
  • Outside Level III services. Examination preparation and grading, procedure approval and certification sign-off under your written practice, without a full-time Level III on payroll.
  • Procedure writing and review. Method procedures aligned to ASME Section V, AWS D1.1 and D1.5, API 1104, and your customers' specifications.
  • Corporate training programmes. Structured development of trainees from Level I to Level II across several methods, delivered onsite.

Book a Level III consultation and we will review your current documentation before recommending anything. Background reading: SNT-TC-1A guidance.

Practise before the practical exam

The Practical NDT 3D simulator lets trainees practise 12 NDT methods in five environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. For Chicago trainees, the oil and gas site and storage tank scenes resemble refinery and terminal work, the welding workshop mirrors fabrication and heavy-equipment shops, and the aircraft hangar suits technicians heading for aviation maintenance.

It is practice, not certification. The simulator does not replace the practical examination on real specimens graded under a Level III, and it does not count as on-the-job experience unless your employer's written practice explicitly says so. Its value is repetition: set-up, scanning coverage, calibration habits and indication recognition before you face the real exam.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. He sets course content and examinations, supervises onsite programmes and works directly with employers on written practices and Level III services.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Chicago

How do I get NDT certified in Chicago?

Under SNT-TC-1A your employer certifies you after you complete formal training, documented experience, general, specific and practical examinations under a Level III, and a vision test. If you are new to NDT, start with Level I training in UT, MT or PT, then apply to Chicagoland inspection contractors, fabricators or plants that will certify you under their written practice.

Can I take NDT training online in Illinois?

Yes, the theory portion for every method and level is available as live online instruction. Hands-on skill development and the practical examination require real equipment and specimens, arranged onsite with your employer or through an employer programme. See online NDT training.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

That depends on your employer's written practice and whether you already hold UT Level I. SNT-TC-1A recommends minimum training hours and experience for each level; the training requirements matrix shows the reference figures. In practice the experience requirement takes longer than the classroom work.

Do I need a license for radiography in Illinois?

Yes. The company needs an IEMA-OHS radioactive materials licence for source radiography, and individuals performing or supervising industrial radiography must hold Illinois radiographer certification. If your work takes you into northwest Indiana, NRC rules apply there instead. SNT-TC-1A RT certification is a separate, employer-issued qualification in technique and interpretation.

What does NDT training cost in Chicago?

We do not publish prices. The quote depends on method, level, number of trainees and whether training is online or onsite at your facility. Quotes are returned within one business day; request your Chicago NDT training quote.

Is ASNT certification recognised by Chicago employers?

SNT-TC-1A is the standard personnel qualification basis for industrial NDT in Chicagoland, used by refinery contractors, fabricators, steel-sector contractors and pipeline contractors. Nuclear plants add their own qualification programmes, and aerospace employers typically apply NAS 410; in both cases SNT-TC-1A training is a valid foundation.

Which NDT method pays off fastest in Chicago?

For refinery and pipeline contractors, UT and RT at Level II. For fabrication, steel and heavy equipment, MT and UT. For aviation, PT and ET. Many technicians start with PT and MT, then add UT, and move into PAUT once they have solid conventional UT experience.

Can you train our crew between turnarounds?

Yes. Onsite programmes are scheduled around your turnaround, outage or production calendar. Many Chicagoland employers use the winter months for classroom and practical training so crews are certified before spring work.

Does Atlantis offer API 510, API 570 or CWI courses in Chicago?

No. Atlantis training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A based only. Some Chicago refineries and fabricators also ask for API inspector certificates or AWS CWI; those are separate schemes run by other bodies.

How do I prepare for the ASNT Level III exams from Chicago?

Level III candidates need substantial experience plus the ASNT Basic and method examinations or an equivalent employer examination. Our ASNT Level III exam preparation covers both, delivered live online. Practice material such as our UT Level 2 practice questions helps at every level.

Will my certification carry over if I switch Chicago employers?

Not automatically. Certification belongs to the employer. Keep your training certificates and experience logs; the new employer's Level III can credit them and re-examine you under their written practice.

Do nuclear plants in Illinois accept SNT-TC-1A training?

Nuclear in-service inspection has additional requirements, including plant qualification programmes and performance demonstration for many UT examinations. SNT-TC-1A training and certification are a common starting point, but the plant or its inspection vendor determines the full qualification.
